title: Q3 2026 Black Mass Price Review
gist: Global black mass payables fell across all regions in Q3 2026 as cobalt sulphate (-33.3% q-o-q) and lithium carbonate (-17.9%) slumped, with high-cobalt LCO material hit hardest (CIF Asia LCO -19.5%). A US rule forcing recyclers to sell 100% of black mass domestically (softened by interim 365-day export licences), tighter EU waste-shipment rules and Indian licensing are fragmenting trade, while liquidity is shifting toward LFP feedstocks.

insights.claim: Benchmark's NCM black mass EXW China payables fell 4.9% in Q3 2026, from 77.0% to 73.3%, while LCO black mass EXW China payables fell to 70.8% for both lithium carbonate and cobalt sulphate (down 7.5% and 13.2% q-o-q respectively).
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Recycler feedstock economics in the largest market are deteriorating, compressing value captured from end-of-life batteries.
insights.quote: NCM Black Mass EXW China payables have fallen 4.9% since the end of Q2, from 77.0% to 73.3%
insights.locator: Benchmark’s NCM Black Mass EXW China payables

insights.claim: Outside China, NCM black mass CIF Asia payables fell 10.4% q-o-q from 120% to 107.5%, while EXW North America and EXW Europe payables dropped 13.6% and 8.3% respectively.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Ex-China payable declines were steeper than in China, hurting Western recycler margins disproportionately.
insights.quote: Benchmark NCM Black Mass CIF Asia payables fell 10.4% q-o-q, from 120% to 107.5%
insights.locator: Benchmark’s NCM Black Mass EXW China payables

insights.claim: Virgin metal prices drove the payable decline: cobalt sulphate, nickel sulphate and lithium carbonate fell 33.3%, 13.0% and 17.9% q-o-q respectively in Q3 2026, squeezing battery recycler margins.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Recycling profitability is a levered derivative of virgin battery metal prices; a one-third cobalt drop cascades straight into feedstock values.
insights.quote: cobalt sulphate, nickel sulphate and lithium carbonate declined -33.3%, -13.0% and -17.9% q-o-q, respectively
insights.locator: Why did Chinese black mass payables keep sliding in Q3?

insights.claim: High-cobalt materials fared worst, with CIF Asia LCO black mass payables falling 19.5% q-o-q and end-of-life LCO dropping from 92.5% to 74.5% as buyers began refusing high-cobalt cargoes.
insights.speaker: Frederick Bloomfield
insights.so_what: Cobalt-rich scrap (consumer electronics) is becoming hard to place, signalling a structural discount on cobalt-bearing feedstocks.
insights.quote: Buyers began to refuse high-Co black mass cargoes, whilst suppliers had to lower offers to offload material.
insights.locator: Again, CIF Asia LCO black mass payables

insights.claim: LFP black mass prices tracked lithium carbonate lower, with the lithium price per percentage point falling from RMB 7,350/tonne at end-June to RMB 6,350/tonne at end-September 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: LFP scrap value is almost a direct lithium price proxy, useful for modelling LFP recycling economics.
insights.quote: the lithium price per percentage point falling from RMB 7,350/tonne at the end of June to RMB 6,350/tonne
insights.locator: LFP black mass prices trended negatively too

insights.claim: Ex-China black mass payables follow Chinese domestic trends with a lag, and by end-Q3 traders were offering material at discounts to sell quickly before further losses, indicating distressed selling.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: China domestic payables can serve as a leading indicator for Western and Asian black mass pricing.
insights.quote: payables mirrored trends in the domestic China market in a lagged manner
insights.locator: What happened to black mass payables outside of China?

insights.claim: Continued weakness in cobalt and lithium prices could keep downward pressure on black mass payables across all regions heading into Q4 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: No near-term relief expected for recycler margins absent a virgin metal rebound.
insights.locator: LFP feedstock trading activity will also be of interest

themes.theme: Export controls fragment black mass trade

insights.claim: The US government issued a temporary ruling, effective 27 August 2026 for at least one year, requiring US recyclers to allocate 100% of monthly black mass sales to US buyers unless granted an exception.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Resource nationalism now extends to battery scrap, aiming to feed domestic hydromet capacity and potentially depressing US feedstock prices.
insights.quote: requiring US recyclers to allocate 100% of monthly black mass sales to US buyers unless granted an exception
insights.locator: How are US black mass export restrictions reshaping flows?

insights.claim: By mid-September 2026, every US recycler that applied for an exemption had received an interim 365-day export licence, allowing Asia-bound black mass shipments to resume, so the rule's near-term bite was limited.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The headline export ban is porous in practice; the real risk is the unresolved final ruling after the interim window.
insights.quote: all domestic recyclers that had applied for exemptions had received interim 365-day export licences
insights.locator: How are US black mass export restrictions reshaping flows?

insights.claim: Increasingly stringent European hazardous waste shipment enforcement, ahead of the European Commission's updated List of Waste deadline, is pushing Asian traders toward second-life cells and battery scrap instead of black mass.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Regulation is reshaping which battery waste forms trade across borders, shifting value to less-processed scrap.
insights.quote: pushing many Asian traders to switch their attention to second life cells and battery scrap
insights.locator: Elsewhere, the application of hazardous waste

insights.claim: In India only a small handful of battery recyclers hold export licences, and they may export only a set portion of production.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: India joins the US and Europe in constraining black mass exports, shrinking the freely tradable pool.
insights.locator: Elsewhere, the application of hazardous waste

insights.claim: Regional fragmentation and cautious procurement intensified after the US intervention, and further trade interventions by other countries following Europe, the US and India could affect the market.
insights.speaker: Frederick Bloomfield
insights.so_what: A regionalised black mass market implies widening regional price spreads and arbitrage opportunities.
insights.quote: the trend towards regional fragmentation and cautious procurement continued following the US government’s regulatory intervention on black mass exports
insights.locator: Throughout Q3 2026, global black mass payables

insights.claim: Western hydrometallurgical capacity build-out is a key watch item following the export restrictions and the US Department of Energy's USD 500m grant commitment to battery and critical mineral recycling.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Policy is steering feedstock and subsidies toward domestic Western hydromet refiners, a potential beneficiary set.
insights.quote: the US Department of Energy’s USD$500m grant commitment to battery and critical mineral recycling
insights.locator: What is next for black mass payables in Q4?

insights.claim: LFP black mass liquidity grew in Q3 2026 as more Asian players shifted attention to LFP feedstocks, lifting prices and making gate fees (where sellers pay recyclers to take material) less common.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: LFP scrap is transitioning from a waste liability to a positively priced commodity, improving LFP end-of-life economics.
insights.quote: with prices going up and gate fees becoming less common
insights.locator: Liquidity for LFP black mass grew

insights.claim: As buying interest in LFP waste streams increases, intensifying competition could produce significant price shifts in LFP feedstock.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Competition for LFP scrap could compress LFP-focused recyclers' input margins even as cobalt feedstock weakens.
insights.quote: there could be significant shifts in the price as competition intensifies
insights.locator: LFP feedstock trading activity will also be of interest
